comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER confirms formal Filosofie (Dutch) and Philosophy (English) tracks. The normalized English-named target and corrected registry ENG attribute are instantiated as the English track, comprising 150 EC of philosophy and 30 EC of genuinely open third-year elective/minor space. Ten 6-EC subjects each form Years 1 and 2. The 2026–27 annual plan requires at least one World Philosophies and the Construction of Traditions I/II restricted-choice module in Year 2 or 3; World Philosophies I is chosen in Year 2. Theoretical Philosophy: Capita Selecta fills the other second-year choice. Year 3 contains a 6-EC Bachelor Seminar III, a 12-EC thesis and two valid 6-EC restricted electives (History of Philosophy: Capita Selecta and Issues in Contemporary Ethics) beside the open 30 EC. Zero-credit first/second-year seminars and language test are excluded from credited components. The VU describes a Dutch track and Dutch PLUS variants under the same bachelor; these are not folded into this English pathway, and the registry ENG-only attribute is narrower than the current bilingual programme description.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized canonical name is Philosophy, the corrected registry attribute lists ENG, and the current adopted OER explicitly names Philosophy as its English track. The distinct Dutch Filosofie track has other variants and a different credit structure, so the exact named track is selected without regard to UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, argument and historical perspectives
alternatives.concept: Combines philosophical ethics, mind and self, political philosophy, logic and persuasion with historical and intercultural interpretation. UCR brings these inquiries together across philosophy, history, literature and communication rather than reproducing VU’s sustained philosophy text seminars or thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains direct philosophy courses and an argumentation strand, complemented by historical and intercultural sources.
progression: Six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, term offerings and formal prerequisites checked against the current enriched workbook; foundation courses precede related advanced work where feasible.

alternatives.label: Ethics, climate and public reasoning
alternatives.concept: Uses philosophical ethics, political philosophy and argumentation to study climate responsibility, market choices, environmental justice and governance. The social-science and sustainability courses are applications of a practical-philosophy question rather than substitutes for VU’s specialist philosophical history and thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Climate Change, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Governance of Sustainability and related communication and economic courses ground the ethical questions in public decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses change from the closest route: Climate Change, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Communicating the Climate Crisis, Introduction to Economics, Governance of Sustainability, Research in a Sustainable Delta and Media & the Environment among them replace historical and literary context, ancient archaeology, rhetoric practice and textual interpretation. The changes shift inquiry from a broad history-and-argument survey to climate, market and governance applications.
progression: Six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, term offerings and formal prerequisites checked against the current enriched workbook; foundation courses precede related advanced work where feasible.

selection.assessment: The closest path answers the broad classical Philosophy core with historical, practical and theoretical questions, logic, argument and interpretation. The climate, markets and governance cluster yields a substantively different UCR programme and is included second. A stand-alone theoretical-philosophy route would repeat all available UCR philosophy of mind, free will and logic courses already used in the closest path; filling the rest with cognitive science and computation would change the field rather than provide a different philosophy curriculum. The Dutch PLUS Religion & Theology variant is official, but UCR lacks a sustained religion or theology sequence for a defensible 24-course route. Production stops at two.

notes.text: VU teaches a sustained 150-EC English philosophy sequence across history, practical and theoretical philosophy, formal restricted choices, philosophical text seminars and a 12-EC independent thesis, with 30 EC of open minor space. UCR offers several philosophy subjects, political philosophy, logic and argumentation, then draws on history, communication and social science for related inquiry. These complementary courses do not amount to VU’s breadth of specialist philosophy or the required thesis. Current VU documents also show a Dutch track within the bachelor even though the registry target records ENG.
